title: You think you’ve gone too far.
paragraphs: You think you’ve gone too far.

Too dirty.
Too numb.
Too far gone to be loved like that.

But then you look at the cross…
and everything you believed about your worth starts to collapse.

Because that love?
It doesn’t stay shallow.
It goes down.
All the way down.
“That you… may have power to comprehend… what is the breadth and length and height and depth.” — Ephesians 3:18
Paul wasn’t exaggerating.
He was struggling to describe something human language can’t contain.

The depth of Christ’s love is not poetic—it’s bloody.
It’s not theory—it’s a cross.
And here’s where it hits:

Jesus didn’t love a cleaned-up version of you.
He didn’t wait for your habits to change.
He didn’t say, “Fix yourself, then I’ll come.”
No.

Romans 5:8 says:
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not after.
Not someday.
While.

That means at your lowest…
your darkest thought…
your secret sin…
your hidden addiction…
your private compromise…
He saw it.
And stayed.
Let that sit for a moment.
Because most people walk away when they see the real you.
But Jesus stepped closer.

Closer to your mess.
Closer to your shame.
Closer to your chains.
Why?

Because His love doesn’t run from brokenness.
It runs toward it.
Christlike love is not soft.

It doesn’t tolerate sin.
It destroys it.

The same love that embraces you…
is the same love that calls you out.

John 8:11 — Jesus tells the woman caught in adultery:
“Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more.”
Did you catch that?

No condemnation.
But also—no compromise.
That’s the depth.
A love that saves you and transforms you.

A love that doesn’t just pull you out of the pit…
but refuses to leave you the same.

So if you say, “Jesus loves me,”
but you’re still clinging to the sin He died to free you from—
That’s not the fullness of His love.
That’s just the part that feels good.

But real love?
It redeems. It corrects. It restores.
And yes—it costs.
It cost Him everything.

The nails.
The crown.
The suffocation.
The silence of heaven as He bore the wrath meant for us.
That’s the depth of His love.

Not just emotional.
Not just comforting.
Sacrificial. Holy. Relentless.
And here’s the invitation most people ignore:
You don’t just receive this love.
You surrender to it.

You let it break your pride.
Expose your sin.
Rebuild your heart.

Because until you do—
you will keep calling lust “love,”
control “care,”
and compromise “freedom.”
But Jesus offers something deeper.

Freedom that’s clean.
Love that’s pure.
Grace that transforms.
And maybe that’s why this hits so hard…
Because deep down, you know:
You don’t need shallow love anymore.

You need the kind of love
that reaches into your darkest places
and doesn’t flinch.
That’s Jesus.
So here’s the question:

Will you stay in hiding…
or will you step into that kind of love?

No more pretending.
No more delaying.
No more half-surrender.
Come back.

Repent—not just feeling sorry, but turning around.
Receive—not just knowing about Jesus, but trusting Him fully.
Because the cross wasn’t the end.
Three days later—He rose.

And that means the same power that conquered the grave…
can break the chains you thought would never fall.
This is your moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Now.

Jesus didn’t just love you at your worst.
He died to give you your best—new life in Him.
